subject: OrchardBridge request: international data protections runbook and DPA annex sign-off
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@orchardbridge.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@orchardbridge.com
Date: 2028-06-25T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: International data protections runbook + DPA annex clarifications

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we discussed on the call, OrchardBridge is pulling together vendor assessment materials for our EU rollout and we need a concise runbook + answers to a few specific cross-border/data protection items so our legal and security teams can sign off. Can you please provide the following by Wednesday EOD (our side deadline):

- Short runbook describing how Redwood handles EU->US transfers for real-time inference (data flow, retention, pseudonymization)
- Confirmation of lawful basis when Redwood acts as a processor for OrchardBridge (GDPR basis)
- Details on DPA annex: options for SCCs/UK Addendum, and whether you support a processor-to-processor transfer scenario
- Proof points: SOC 2, encryption in transit & at rest, KMS/HSM, key rotation cadence
- List of subprocessors and their data residency (if any)

We may need a redlined DPA annex; I can route to our procurement/legal once we have the draft. Please include any supporting artifacts as attachments or links.

Regards,
Sarah Liu
Head of Security and Privacy
OrchardBridge Health

P.S. Our legal lead (copied) may ask a few deeper technical questions about your KV cache and model caching behavior — any notes you can include up front would be helpful.

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@orchardbridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@orchardbridge.com
Date: 2028-06-25T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: International data protections runbook + DPA annex clarifications

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise runbook and a draft DPA annex for your review. High level answers below; Monica and Karthik are looped for specifics and the subprocessor list.

- Lawful basis: Redwood acts as a processor for customer-provided personal data; we rely on the controller's lawful basis. We document this in the DPA annex and map processing activities.
- Transfers: We support SCCs (EU Commission and UK Addendum where applicable). For US-hosted inference we provide supplemental transfer safeguards described in the runbook (technical and contractual).
- Encryption: TLS in transit; at-rest encryption using customer KMS options for Dedicated/Private; hosted accounts use AES-256 with managed KMS; HSM-backed key management available for enterprise plans.
- Subprocessors: attached CSV; we maintain notification cadence and a public registry link.

Request: Monica will provide the technical appendix that addresses KV cache behavior, pseudonymization and retention profiles for model inference. If you need a DocuSign-ready annex please confirm the signatory details and we'll push the envelope.

Next steps I propose:
1) Monica provides the technical appendix by EOD tomorrow
2) Your legal reviews draft annex and flags redlines
3) We iterate on DocuSign package

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPF_Runbook.pdf, DPA_Annex_OrchardBridge.docx

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@orchardbridge.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@orchardbridge.com
Date: 2028-06-26T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: International data protections runbook + DPA annex clarifications

Hi Sarah / Logan — attaching the technical appendix and quick Q&A that maps directly to OrchardBridge's checklist. Key points below (summarized):

1) Data flows and retention- For real-time inference, customer input is accepted via API and routed transiently to the serving runtime. We support two retention profiles:
  * ephemeral (default): inputs and generated tokens retained in-memory only for the duration of the request; KV cache entries not persisted to disk unless explicitly enabled; TTL per-customer configurable (default 0).
  * short-term cache: optional KV cache to improve latency; cache keys are pseudonymized, and values can be configured to avoid storing raw PII. Retention TTLs configurable (1h / 24h / 7d).

2) Lawful basis and DPA annex- Redwood is a processor. The DPA annex includes a controller-designated lawful basis section for you to fill (we do not assert controller status). We support SCCs; if OrchardBridge requires an alternative transfer mechanism we can discuss additional contractual safeguards.

3) Subprocessors & data residency- Full list attached (Subprocessor_List.csv) and we maintain a public registry link for region-specific infra. For Dedicated/Private customers we offer region isolation and on-prem packages when required.

4) Encryption & key management- Hosted: AES-256 at rest with managed KMS; Dedicated/Private: customer-managed KMS or HSM integration (PKCS#11), with key rotation supported on a quarterly or custom schedule. We can provision an HSM-backed key for DPA Annex customers on our enterprise plan.

5) KV cache and model caching (specific to your security team's ask)- KV cache is implemented to reduce repeated prefix computation; by default it stores only tokenized embeddings and truncated context segments. We do not persist full request payloads unless customer enables persistent cache. For customers requiring stricter controls we offer:
  * cache isolation per-tenant (no cross-tenant lookups)
  * optional in-memory-only mode (no disk spill)
  * audit hooks that log cache hits/misses without storing payloads

6) Auditability & evidence- SOC 2 Type II report (latest), pen-test summary, and dataflow diagrams attached. We also provide change logs for subprocessor updates and quarterly transfer impact assessments on request.

7) Implementation notes for DocuSign- We can prepare a DocuSign-ready DPA annex with placeholders for your controller details and signatory. Provide the full legal entity name, address, and primary signatory email and we'll send the envelope.

Attachments included: Redwood_DPF_Runbook.pdf (runbook and dataflow map), DPA_Annex_OrchardBridge.docx (draft annex), Subprocessor_List.csv (current as of 2028-06-24).

Let me know if you want a short tech call to walk the security team through the runbook tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Principal, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: International data protections runbook + DPA annex clarifications

Monica — thanks for the thorough appendix and attachments, these look good and answer most of our questions. A couple quick follow-ups from our security team before we escalate to legal: 

1) For hosted accounts: how is key rotation handled for managed KMS? What rotation window do you enforce and can we require a custom rotation cadence?
2) For the HSM option: can you confirm FIPS level and whether keys are exportable?
3) We need explicit language in the DPA annex about in-memory-only cache mode (we'll include the desired TTL). Can you add a short paragraph we can rely on for sign-off?

If you can reply with short bullet answers on those three items and send the DocuSign envelope to legal@orchardbridge.com (signatory: Daniel Reyes, General Counsel) we'll aim to complete review this week.

Best,
Sarah Liu
Head of Security and Privacy
OrchardBridge Health
